chapter_title: Concerning the Fourteen Vehicles that Jesus has boarded.
chapter_note: ¶2–8 preserve a compact, systematic correspondential list of ten cosmic “vehicles” (ships, pillar, summons/obedience, and five living elements) used to describe Jesus’ descent through the cosmological architecture. The chapter then shows strong editorial fatigue: ¶9 is a clear institutional graft (“holy church…brothers…sisters…catechumens”), and ¶10 is a homiletic/doxological summary with a beatitude rather than further cosmological mapping.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic scene-setting (“Once again… speaks… to the congregation”) is the compiling community’s hagiographic frame, not part of the teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: When Jesus the Son of Greatness came to these worlds, at the time that he unveiled the greatness, he boarded ten vehicles. He journeyed in the universe by them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological exposition introducing a numbered structure (ten vehicles) within the system. Despite the name “Jesus,” this is Jesus-as-cosmic-being, not a Gospel citation.

paragraphs.core_text: The first vehicle is the light ship, since he received instructions from the Ambassador there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: List-item cosmological mapping (vehicle → cosmic location/relationship) stays entirely within the Manichaean cosmic hierarchy (Ambassador).

paragraphs.core_text: The second carriage is the ship of the First Man, since his dwelling is established there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic enumerated mapping; “First Man” and his ship are core cosmological actors/structures. (Manuscript page marker removed.)

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man, since he shone forth there. He came below, he appeared in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-station identification in numbered sequence; “Pillar of Glory/Perfect Man” functions as cosmological architecture in the descent schema.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the summons that he clothed upon his body. The fifth is the obedience that he swathed upon the summons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic Manichaean redemptive mechanics expressed as correspondential ‘clothing’ (summons/obedience) without audience-address or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth is the living air, and since he assumed it too, he received anointment there. The seventh is the living wind that blows. The eighth is the light that illuminates. The ninth is the living water. The tenth is the living fire that is above them all.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Five-fold elemental sequence (living air/wind/light/water/fire) in a fixed enumerated structure—highly characteristic of the old systematic layer.

paragraphs.core_text: He was journeying in these ten carriages among all the orders and all the [...], those above and those below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Wraps the tenfold scheme in universal cosmic scope (“orders…above…below”) still wholly internal to the cosmological system; retains lacuna.

Editorial seam/extension: the mapping crosses cosmos→institution (“holy church…brothers…sisters…catechumens”), applying the scheme to contemporary community structure rather than describing what cosmic things are.

Homiletic/doxological closure: moralizing salvation language, victory over ‘strangers,’ praise, and a beatitude (“Blessed is he…”) signal later pastoral framing rather than continued systematic cosmological mapping.
